pullRequest.title: feat(probe-schema): accept the J07 launcher identity facts

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail J07 when launcher identity is absent**

When a report omits `launcher_identity` or supplies `null`, this branch silently skips the new identity gate, so all remaining J07 checks can pass without proving that the launcher is the expected shebang process. This also preserves old probe reports through the schema and `serde(default)` fallback; treat absent identity as a failure and make the contract breaking rather than bypassing the check.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L13-L13](https://github.com/jackin-project/jackin/blob/54bd572d2a9537ca3be2426e42427603c896bad2/AGENTS.md#L13-L13)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:64` still gates the whole identity block on `if let Some(identity) = &facts.launcher_identity`, so an absent/null `launcher_identity` still passes J07. This matches the signed contract: the sentinel probe emits `launcher_identity=null` whenever the launcher is not a shebang script or the cross-check fails (jackin-sentinel `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:2294-2296`), and `rewrite/probe-schema.json:818-826` keeps the field nullable for exactly that reason. Making absence a failure is a cross-repo contract change against jackin-sentinel#160 and is left to the author/operator. Not resolved.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require and compare launcher start-time evidence**

For the raw `/proc/PID/stat` evidence, zero-based `nth(2)` reads field 3—the process state—not field 22's start time, and the entire comparison is skipped when `stat_pre` is null. Two unrelated processes commonly have the same state, such as `S`, so a replaced or PID-reused launcher can pass this purported pre-launch identity binding; require `stat_pre` and compare the parsed start-time field.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- After fmt/clippy the comparison is at `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:119-121` and still compares `split_whitespace().nth(2)` (process state) and is still skipped when `stat_pre` is null. Correcting the field index (start time is field 22) is a judging-semantic change outside the scope of this CI-gate fix. Not resolved.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject a missing launcher comm value**

When `launcher_identity.comm` is null while `processes.main` exists, this conditional performs no validation, even though the schema explicitly permits that null value. A partial identity record can therefore pass without binding its recorded command name to the observed main process; reject a missing or empty `comm` before comparing it with `main.comm`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:98-104` still compares `comm` with `processes.main.comm` only when both are `Some`; a null `comm` is not rejected. Not resolved by this delivery.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cross-check the executable against the resolved interpreter**

When a probe emits contradictory evidence such as `exe_matches_interpreter: true` while `exe` differs from `interpreter_resolved`, this code accepts it because it trusts the derived boolean and checks the two paths only for non-emptiness. A probe regression can therefore make J07 pass even though the recorded running executable identifies the wrong interpreter; compare the resolved paths directly or otherwise reject inconsistent records.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:65-69` still trusts `checks.exe_matches_interpreter` and only requires `exe` to be non-empty (`:92-93`); it does not compare `exe` with `interpreter_resolved`. Not resolved by this delivery.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify that the launcher runs as the sandbox user**

When the launcher runs under an unexpected account, such as UID 0, a nonempty `uid` value still satisfies this check. J04 verifies the separately executed probe and host command are UID 1000, not the already-running main process, so J07 can pass while `jackin-start` itself is privileged; parse this field and require the expected sandbox UID.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:95-96` still only requires a non-empty `uid`; it does not parse the value or compare it with the expected sandbox UID. Not resolved by this delivery.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind launcher evidence to the selected main PID**

When more than one `jackin-start`-named process exists, `LauncherIdentity` can describe a different process from `facts.processes.main`: it carries no typed PID, and the judge compares only the command name. Matching names and internally consistent stat snapshots from a decoy can therefore pass while the host process and agent checks concern another PID; carry or parse the PID and start time from `stat_before` and require them to equal `main.pid` and `main.start_ticks`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Fixed and pushed: 2d17ddab3 (cargo fmt), b7295bb4c (clippy: the five boolean verdicts are now grouped in the flattened `LauncherIdentityChecks`/`LauncherArgvMatches` sub-structs, wire format unchanged), af906be3e (schema-contract test). Those commits fix the CI gates only and do not change the J07 judging semantics or the flat wire format, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- `LauncherIdentity` is regrouped at `crates/xtask/src/e2e/probe.rs:484-512` (`LauncherIdentityChecks` + `LauncherArgvMatches`, flattened so the flat JSON of `rewrite/probe-schema.json` `$defs/LauncherIdentity` and of the sentinel output `probe/jackin-sentinel-probe:519-525` is byte-identical), but it still carries no PID and `judge_agent` still binds only the comm. Adding a field would change the frozen cross-repo wire format. Not resolved.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify stability from the recorded stat snapshots**

When `stat_before` and `stat_after` identify different PIDs or start times but the report sets `stable: true`, this check accepts the contradictory evidence because the snapshots are only checked for non-emptiness. That lets a launcher replacement during sampling pass J07; parse the PID and start-time fields from both snapshots and compare them rather than trusting the derived boolean alone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Pushed fixes (2d17ddab3 cargo fmt, b7295bb4c clippy grouping, af906be3e schema-contract test) repair the CI gates only and do not change J07 judging semantics, so this finding is **not** satisfied by them:

- After fmt/clippy the check is at `crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:126-128` and still trusts the derived `checks.stable` boolean; `stat_before`/`stat_after` are only required non-empty (`crates/xtask/src/e2e/steps/j07.rs:105-116`). Deriving stability from the parsed snapshots is a judging-semantic change outside the scope of this CI-gate fix. Not resolved.
